notes: Coordinates: removed a stray empty circle under the address boxes (it was the hidden spot for address errors showing when it shouldn't).
Every page: the page's description now sits to the right of its title.
Settings: a gear at the bottom of the sidebar opens the settings (Blender and Charon Forge for corvette covers), instead of Cover settings on the Garage and Dock Yard.
Shipwright: LiveLink sits under the corvette's picture, and Copy all, Paste all, Load file, Load from a .blend and Save as are on one line.
Coordinates: You are here is a slimmer bar with Start from here beside it, and Favourite places opens and closes.

Dock Yard: the view and action buttons are one row, the type and tag filters sit beside Cover Flow / Grid, the ship count is under the title, a corvette build offers Copy corvette, and favourites are a star (filled when it's a favourite).
Shipwright: LiveLink has its own box under the corvette list.

Shipwright: the corvette's picture is as tall as the cards beside it, and its picture options sit behind a gear in its corner (also on the Starships, Multi-tools, Freighter, Exocraft and Companions pictures).
Shipwright: Copy all sits with Paste all, Load file, Load from a .blend and Save as.
Shipwright: Parts opens and closes like Build JSON.
Overview: Quick fixes now opens and closes with a click, and holds the repair, recharge and fill buttons together with your units, nanites and quicksilver.
Overview: play time, starships, multi-tools, bases and the save version are now part of Journey.
Overview: your traveller's picture options (choose a screenshot, import an image, go back to the default) sit behind the gear on the portrait.

LiveLink: natural joints now follow a person's range of movement. Elbows bend forwards and knees backwards and both can twist a little; the neck, back, shoulders, hips, wrists and ankles move freely within a natural range; fingers still bend like hinges. Turn Natural joints off to move any joint any way.
Traveller page: a new loading mark (the Harmonious logo, its orbs circling the star) shows over the ship while Blender makes its 3D model or renders it.
Traveller page: a note under the picture says the page is still experimental, with a link to Discord to report problems.
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.15.0).

Traveller page: Render this angle. Turn your corvette's 3D model to the angle you like, press Render this angle, and Blender renders it from exactly that angle with all its textures and colours, in the same spot on the picture. Rendered angles stay in the Angle list.
Traveller page: the corvette's 3D model is lighter and faster to turn, shows its real surface pictures, and no longer has white sheets where the game has see-through panels.

Traveller page: corvettes now turn in 3D like your traveller, with no Blender for you to open. Pick a corvette and the editor builds its 3D model in the background with your Blender and Charon Forge (a minute or two the first time; it's kept after that). Then turn it with the middle mouse button.
Traveller: fingers no longer stretch or warp when you move them one at a time; each piece of a finger now moves as one.
Traveller page: move anything anywhere, even right off the picture. Bring back (in each box) or Bring everything into the picture (under Size) puts it back.
Traveller page: thinner frame round the picture.
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.14.0).

Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.13.0): each hand's two fingers now move one at a time, Natural joints (on by default) make fingers, elbows and knees bend the way real ones do at their own joint, and Body parts has Hands sliders from open to a fist
LiveLink: Send the corvette in 3D (Builds panel) sends a corvette's model to the Traveller page, where it turns like your traveller
Traveller page: new space backgrounds (Eclipse, Blue nebula, Violet clouds, Meteor storm, Ringed planets) beside the starfield
Traveller page: things can go past the edges of the picture (only the head showing, say) and be made bigger
Traveller page: 3D poses, ships and multi-tools are sharper, with the game's surface detail
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.12.0): the new round LiveLink logo at the top, and coloured icons: neon pink for building corvettes and bases, neon blue for posing your traveller
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.11.0): the Picture box lists your lights with Power and Colour; clicking one leaves Pose mode and selects it, so G moves it and R turns it

Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.10.0): the Picture and 3D panel has Quality (Quick, or Best with Cycles for real light, soft shadows and reflections), ready-made Lighting (Studio, Hero, Sunset, Space, or keep your own lights) and Lenses and screens glow
Traveller page: Lighting for 3D (Studio, Hero, Sunset, Space) in the Background box, and glowing lenses and screens from Blender glow on the picture too

Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.9.0): each part of LiveLink is now its own panel you can open and close (Builds, Your traveller, Poses, Body parts, Multi-tool, Picture and 3D), and Your traveller has Pose the traveller / Done posing, so Base Builder's tools come back when you finish posing
Traveller page: a new layout with boxes you open and close: Size (with Custom width and height), Traveller, Ship, Multi-tool, Background, Text and Portal glyphs
Traveller page: put a multi-tool on the picture, import your own image for the traveller or ship, remove an image's background, and choose which layer sits in front
Traveller page: drag with the middle mouse button to turn a 3D pose, ship or multi-tool (Shift and the middle button moves it, as in Blender)
Traveller page: new space backgrounds (nebula, ringed planet, shooting stars, galaxy), plain colours with presets, fonts for your name, and a logo
Traveller page: pictures carry a small watermark in the corner; patrons can take it off by signing in with Patreon

Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.8.0): Your traveller has a new Body parts section (closed until you open it) where you pick the head, torso, arms, hands, legs, backpack, chest piece and cape, or the whole traveller; pick several at once and R turns each at its own joint

Traveller page: Render the angles now shows what Blender is doing, renders the corvette's cover for its current build first when it's missing, and shows the front when the angles are ready (before, the new angles didn't appear until you picked the ship again)
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.7.0): it can now put one of your multi-tools in your traveller's hand (Your traveller, Multi-tool, Hold it), and it stays there in every pose
Traveller page: starships and multi-tools show the game's model with its textures in the ship's own colours
Traveller page: a ship or corvette with your own picture can switch between your picture and the 3D model or the corvette's renders, so the angles still work
Traveller page: Render the angles makes a corvette's front, side, back and top renders when it only has its cover
Traveller page: click something on the picture and press Remove from the picture (or Delete) to take it off
Traveller page: In front of your traveller sits on one line
About fits without scrolling sideways
Save list: light and dark mode is an icon in the bottom-right corner
Traveller page: In front of your traveller puts the ship in front instead of behind

Traveller page in 3D: in Blender press Send the pose to the editor and your posed traveller arrives in 3D, with its textures; turn and tilt it on the card with the sliders or by dragging with Shift held
Traveller page: starships and multi-tools without a picture show their 3D model and can be turned too; corvettes can use any of their render angles
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.6.0)
The Blender add-on buttons are now called LiveLink
Traveller page: a pose you save in Blender while the page is open goes on the card by itself, and a newer pose picture always replaces the one from last time

New Traveller page: make a picture of your posed traveller with a background (starfield, colours, your screenshots or any image), your ship, portal glyphs and your name; drag things to move them, scroll to resize, then save or copy it
The Blender add-on can now be had from the save list, About, Exosuit and the Traveller page (not just Shipwright); it's saved to your Exports folder

Blender: ready-made poses for your traveller (standing, hands on hips, waving, pointing, salute, arms raised, thinking, sitting on a seat, sitting on the ground, kneeling, T-pose); pick one and press Pose
Blender: Save my pose keeps your own poses in Documents\Harmonious Save Editor\Poses; they fit any traveller, so you can share them
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.5.0)
Blender: clicking your traveller's head now picks the neck, so the head turns where it joins the body instead of round the top of the helmet
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.4.1)
Blender: your traveller is now painted in your own colours and markings from your save, the way the game paints them
Exosuit: Save traveller files for the developer also lists the game's colour-layer files, for the next step: your own colours on the model in Blender
Blender: your traveller now comes with the game's own textures (colour, surface detail, metal and rough parts); switch Blender to Material Preview or Rendered to see them
Exosuit: Save traveller files for the developer also collects the colour layers, for the next step: the colours you picked in the game
Blender: bones keep your traveller's proportions, so moving or scaling can't stretch an arm or a leg (turn off Keep the body's proportions in the panel to move bones freely)
Exosuit: Save traveller files for the developer collects your traveller's materials and textures, for the work on real colours and textures
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.4.0)
Blender: clicking on your traveller no longer shows an error in Blender 5, and the bones now stay hidden until you click a part
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.3.1)
Blender: your traveller's bones now sit where they join the body, so a finger, hand or leg turns at the joint instead of swinging through the air

Blender: the bones stay hidden until you click a part of the body; the bone that moves it shows, ready to turn with R (Shift+click adds another, a click on empty space hides them, Show every stick shows them all)
Please install the LiveLink add-on again (version 1.3.0) to get the click-to-pose

Blender add-on 1.2.2: Import my traveller goes straight into Pose mode (click a bone and press R) and shows plain bones instead of spheres. From now on the add-on tells you in Blender when a newer one is ready. Get it on Shipwright and install it over the old one.

Blender add-on: Import my traveller now shows a clean skeleton, without the big spheres on every bone, and hides the game's helper joints (cameras, effects) in a Helpers bone collection. Get the add-on again on Shipwright and install it over the old one.
Exosuit: your traveller, built from your save and your game files with exactly the parts you wear. Export for Blender (.glb) saves them with their skeleton, ready to pose.

New Blender add-on: Your traveller in the LiveLink panel. Import my traveller brings your character in to pose, and Save the pose as a picture renders it to a transparent PNG. Get the add-on again on Shipwright and install it over the old one.
Blender add-on fix: Support the creator now starts closed and the LiveLink panel starts open (they were the wrong way round).

Companions: a Creature battles panel to change a companion's type (greyed out for species the game fixes, such as robots) and set its health, agility and combat effectiveness classes, or make them all S class.
Blender add-on: Support the creator now starts closed; click it to open. Press Get the Blender add-on on Shipwright and install it over the old one to get it.
Updates now come from the editor's Releases page on GitHub, where every version is listed.
Tune-up order: big part counts get thousands separators.
Blender add-on: Support the creator now also links to the Portal Glyph Banner and Traveller credentials makers. Press Get the Blender add-on on Shipwright and install it over the old one to get it.
Shipwright: the gear beside Tune up lets you set your own tune-up order. Move the groups with the arrows or drag them; Standard order puts TAZmd's order back.
New Blender add-on: the LiveLink panel now shows the LiveLink logo and a Support the creator section. Press Get the Blender add-on on Shipwright and install it over the old one to get it.
About: What's new and Check for updates sit on one line under the version.
After an update, the editor now shows what's new (like this).
About shows which version you're using, with a What's new link for recent changes.
A little more room above LiveLink in Shipwright.

The editor now has its own window: closing it asks to Save & exit, and the taskbar shows the editor's icon (re-pin it once if you'd pinned the old one). Also: favourite places, nicknames and a star chart on Coordinates.
Nicknames: give systems and planets your own names, shown only in the editor (they don't rename anything in the game).
In space, You are here shows the star with its planets and moons going round it.
Star a system or any of its planets straight from the Coordinates prediction.
Systems and planets show the names players gave them (from your save), with the game's own name beside them.
Your planet's moon is no longer cut off, and the globe turns even with Windows animation effects off.
Warp here asks how you arrive (ship, freighter or a base); one Places here list; a turning globe of your planet; corvette covers keep their render after a change.
Favourite places: star bases, space stations, settlements and systems on Coordinates and Bases, then pick one and warp there from any save.
Save & exit: the new Exit button, and Cancel on the 'Leave app?' box, offer Save & exit, Exit without saving or Keep editing.
Right-click any inventory slot for a menu: fill, repair, copy, paste, duplicate, supercharge, move to another inventory, remove. Works on selections too.

Adding items: cargo takes anything, and each technology grid only offers technology that fits it (exosuit, multi-tool, freighter, each kind of ship and exocraft). The item library rebuilds once to learn the categories.
Add items by name: click an empty slot in any inventory, type (Carbon, Orbital Exocraft Materialiser…), press Enter or click, and it goes in as a full stack. Technology grids offer only technology.
Dock Yard: ships added since the save was opened (like a new corvette) now show up, and everything you save to the game is kept in the Hangar.
Customise the sidebar: drag pages up, down or into another group, move groups, and hide pages you don't use (button at the bottom of the sidebar).
Dock Yard: every loaded ship shows Loaded, slot N (the first cover could miss it), and loaded ships come first in slot order. Shipwright shows the corvette's picture.

Names: the cover page is now the Garage, and the Dock Yard's automatic copies are the Hangar. Dock Yard ships in your save say Loaded, slot N on the cover, and Load ship into game puts one in. Page buttons sit above the covers, on the left. Supercharge slots on multi-tools and the freighter.

Dock Yard: pick a ship to Edit it (opens Starships, or Shipwright for a corvette's build), put it in your save, or open its details. Cards show which ships are in this save. Starships has Versions in the Dock Yard.
User guide and README updated: companion models, where exports go, pinning to the taskbar, Dock Yard folders, moving ships to the Dock Yard, rewards that won't claim.
Taskbar: the editor keeps its own icon when pinned (Edge was putting its own back).
The editor gets its own taskbar button and icon instead of Edge's.
Companions: every companion's model is found now (Metal Orb, robot pets and the rest), and each is drawn with exactly the head, wings and tail pieces it has.
Companions are drawn from your game's own creature models, with the parts each one was born with (new: tell me if one looks wrong). Dock Yard folder box is clearer.
Dock Yard folders: the path box no longer shows an example that looks like a real folder, and Add path with an empty box opens Browse.
Companions can have a picture (a screenshot or any image) on their page and beside their name in the list.

Ship and multi-tool covers stay drawn when you switch pages and show straight away the next time you open the editor; the Dock Yard fills in every cover by itself. The editor now remembers light or dark mode (and your other settings) every time it opens.

Exports now save to Documents\Harmonious Save Editor\Exports and open that folder (they used to vanish into Downloads). A ship's Dock Yard button can now move it out of your save into Ship storage, freeing the slot.
You can now delete a multi-tool (or ship) when every slot is in use, for example to make room to claim a reward.
Pages no longer slide sideways under the sidebar: a title glow made every page a little wider than the window.

Rewards: the page now explains how to get rewards into the game (quit the game first, save, then start it), Unlock all leaves out the platform rewards the game removes on PC, and the editor tells you if the game puts its own rewards back.
